Writing glass styles... The `.glass-pill` class will override those variables cleanly, following the same pattern as `.glass-lit`. The pill currently has both an inset ring border and the `.glass` border creating a doubled edge, which might contribute to how flat it reads, but I'll keep the inset ring since that's what the spec calls for in clipping contexts.

The inset shadow with `inset 0 1px 0` already gives that brighter top rim to sell the glass effect, so I'm ready to implement this.

- /* Glass with a light of its own behind it, the way the music bar is lit by the
-    cover of whatever is playing.
+ /* The dictation pill, which is the one panel in the app that floats over another
+    application rather than over Crew. Nothing can blur what is back there: a
+    backdrop filter samples the page it is drawn in, and behind this window there
+    is no page, so the tint is the whole of the material and a heavier blur buys
+    nothing at all.
+ 
+    So it is lit the way the app icon is lit instead: the tint falls from a lighter

+    lets it sit this far off opaque without reading as a dark film laid over the

step.text:
Looking at the Windows mouse event handling issue for Q3: when `forward: true` is set, it only sends `WM_MOUSEMOVE` events with no virtual keys pressed, which means Chromium receives mousemove/pointermove events with `buttons: 0` but never gets the corresponding `pointerup` event. This leaves in-flight drag operations stranded without proper completion.

On the `ignore=true` side, Windows applies `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT | WS_EX_LAYERED` flags which exclude the entire window from hit-testing. Meanwhile on macOS, `setIgnoresMouseEvents:` has a similar effect, but there's ambiguity about whether `acceptsMouseMovedEvents` still delivers mouse-moved events when the window is set to ignore mouse events.

The key issue is that Electron's native window code calls `setIgnoresMouseEvents:NO` at construction, which according to the loom workaround is what broke transparent click-through in the first place. I need to verify whether this is still happening in the current version and check if macOS transparent window click-through actually works today given the documented limitation that you can't click through transparent areas.

On Windows, the situation is different — when a BrowserWindow is transparent, Electron sets the WS_EX_LAYERED flag, and Windows hit-testing on layered windows respects alpha values, allowing clicks through fully transparent regions. This explains why issue 30744 shows Windows does pass clicks through, contradicting the general documentation statement.

I need to verify how `layered_` is actually implemented in the source code and check whether this behavior still holds in current Electron versions.

### @estoykov (2025-09-05T16:10:17Z)
I found this
[6106730: [Win] Use DXGI swapchains and DCOMP visuals in software mode](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6106730)

The merge seems to be from January 2025, so it is unclear (at least for me) why this is in effect since Chromium 139.
May be it could be "disabled" (if possible) and force Chromium to use GDI transfer again - which supports mouse click through transparency.

**Edit**: Well, walking around the code from the above commit, the following will allow mouse click over transparent areas with Electron 38.0.0 (Chromium 140.0.7339.41), i.e. will use GDI to draw the page content:

`app.commandLine.appendSwitch("disable-direct-composition");`
`app.disableHardwareAcceleration();`

Hinted from:

> // If direct composition is disabled say for testing, we will use an ANGLE
> // EGLSurface which uses a BitBlt swap chain that needs a redirection surface.
>
